differences.what: The pictured tapering shaft, railed gallery, framed lantern cage, rounded dome and finial are present in the exact-current native render. This is the delivered source-shaped form, not the older opaque drum/pyramid. Exact member counts and metric sections remain declared reconstructions.

The interpreted dark shaft apertures are present. This small print does not independently resolve pane joinery, every face, every count, or an additional metric offset; no visitor-noticeable missing opening or independent displacement is established in this governing view. Other mapped views retain their separate review limits.

Small finial/crown/gallery edge and framing offsets are inside the coarse source readings (finial about y38±3, gallery about y89±2) and retained camera uncertainty. No independent greater than about 0.3 m geometry error is established by those pixels.

The partly hidden shaft toe, foundation/grade, underside and unseen faces are not resolved by the foliage and print. The nominal forty-foot historical datum is not identified as shaft/gallery/finial height. Neither source nor this comparison proves an error from nominal 12.19 m versus reconstructed 12.84968 m top.

This monochrome/aged print does not establish literal pigment, photometric reflectance, exact masonry unit bond, glass opacity or metal colour. The existing neutral stone tones, joints and lantern sections remain reconstructed; no historical colour/material claim is promoted.

The neutral single-tower review omits fort buildings, ships, vegetation, water, terrain and people. Those are scene context, not missing parts of this tower. It does not prove a historical viewing location or every fitting on 1 July 1835.

The seven held compositions were directly reviewed in docs/RESEARCH/lighthouse-picture-signoff-T-2373/REVIEW.md. Baker’s stylized pointed cap conflicts with Castelnau/Andreas; Kellogg’s lower dark aperture and broader shaft/gallery conflict with this governing drawing. The existing lower aperture was separately seen in one actual diagnostic. These are explicit conflicting-picture readings under T-3153, not literal matches to those drawings or independently measured geometry errors.

Andreas, the school shore drawing, the 1849 flood and Peck’s retrospective painting leave tiny, hidden or uncalibrated features unresolved. Their original source/date/rights limits remain; unresolved details are not promoted into extra counts, geometry, historical camera positions or dated alterations.
